gen-fs-bonny-montserrat: Refined is the first word that comes to mind for Bonny, with its mellow shift from thick to thin and tightly packed lines. And Montserrat adds wide, generous e and a shapes in a plain sans that glides along, so Bonny earns its place big and brief.
gen-fs-bonny-roboto-slab: Bonny has a literary, softly modulated look that feels refined. Its curves gape a little and the lines sit tight, while Roboto Slab holds the middle of each line with sturdy, open-throated slab-serif letters that feel precise and structured.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-bespoke-sans: Boxing looks bent from wire, bold and full of energy. Big and brief is where it pays off, while Bespoke Sans stays sharp and refined with plenty of space between curve ends and stems, made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-roundo: Loud, wire-like bowls and stems of one weight give Boxing its punch, with generous space around every letter. Roundo takes over for the quieter work, with its n arch matching its stem and small counters that never clog in a plain sans.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-synonym: Synonym reads as a clean, dependable stripe of ink in a sans with open curves. Boxing is the one to bring energy, with bold, loosely spaced letters, while Synonym is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-boxing-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, with no swelling where a curve turns and a c and s held widely apart. Boxing brings the energy, earning its keep big and short with bold, generously spaced letters.
gen-fs-britney-cabin: Britney writes in a relaxed, calligraphic hand, with letters tucked close and curves as fine as a drawn thread. And Cabin gives it a warm, clean footing in bent-tubing sans-serif forms; enlarge it a touch so its open terminals can breathe.
gen-fs-britney-fs-bespoke-sans: Britney flows in a relaxed calligraphic hand, with no hairlines at all. Bespoke Sans is what makes the pair work, its sharp, refined sans-serif letters leaving generous space between curve ends and stems for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-britney-fs-literata: Expressive and relaxed, Britney draws a plain, unshaded line that never swells. Literata does the opposite job, with sturdy thin lines against slightly heavier thick ones that feel alive in a serif with open mouths, though not for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-britney-fs-roundo: Roundo reads neutral and geometric, its n arch matching the stem and its small counters staying unclogged. Make Britney small and its tight calligraphic hand turns fussy, or enlarge the sans-serif body and it loses its comfort in small doses.
